_comment: Stellaris slang, abbreviations and shorthand a new player meets in the UI, tooltips and community. term -> plain-language meaning. Used by stellaris_glossary.

entries.FE: Fallen Empire - a dormant ancient mega-empire already on the map at game start. Ignores you until you annoy it or it wakes up.
entries.AE: Awakened Empire - a Fallen Empire that has woken up and starts conquering the galaxy. Usually the mid-game alarm bell.
entries.GC: Galactic Community - the mid/late-game galactic senate where empires vote on Resolutions that apply galaxy-wide.
entries.GDF: Galactic Defense Force - a fleet raised by the Galactic Community (or by the Imperium) to fight a crisis.
entries.Custodian: An empire elected by the Galactic Community with emergency powers. Can be made permanent as the Imperium.
entries.Imperium: Permanent Custodianship - the Galactic Community becomes your hereditary empire. Everybody else gets upset.
entries.Ecum: Ecumenopolis - a planet completely paved into one giant city. Massive job output, massive upkeep.
entries.Ring World: A megastructure: four 25-tile artificial worlds with 100% habitability for everyone.
entries.Dyson Sphere: Megastructure that generates enormous amounts of Energy Credits from a star.
entries.Science Nexus: Megastructure that generates large amounts of all three research types.
entries.Matter Decompressor: Megastructure built over a black hole that produces Minerals.
entries.Sentry Array: Megastructure that reveals the whole galaxy (intel on everyone).
entries.Strategic Coordination Center: Megastructure that raises naval capacity and gives a command-limit aura.
entries.Quantum Catapult: Megastructure that flings fleets across the map. Range shown as a projected arc.
entries.Habitat: A space station you can colonise and build districts on. Core of Void Dwellers / tall play.
entries.Void Dwellers: Origin: you start on habitats and live there. Habitat habitability bonus, planet penalty.
entries.Shattered Ring: Origin: start on a broken Ring World you can repair one section of at a time.
entries.Remnants: Origin: start on a relic world full of blockers you can clear for bonuses.
entries.Scion: Origin: start as the subject of a Fallen Empire that protects you until the mid-game.
entries.Lost Colony: Origin: your species was seeded by another empire that is on the map somewhere.
entries.Necrophage: Origin / civic: convert other pops into your species. Requires raising pops to feed you.
entries.Clone Army: Origin: limited pop growth, strong soldiers, big ascension decisions later.
entries.Fanatic Purifiers: Genocidal civic: cannot do diplomacy, gets big bonuses, everyone hates you.
entries.Devouring Swarm: Genocidal hive-mind civic: eat pops for pop growth.
entries.Determined Exterminator: Genocidal machine civic: purge all organics.
entries.Driven Assimilator: Machine civic that cyborg-ifies conquered pops instead of purging them.
entries.Rogue Servitor: Machine civic: keeps organics as pampered Bio-Trophies for Unity. Lose them and you lose.
entries.Gestalt: Hive Mind or Machine Intelligence - no factions, no elections, different economy and ethics.
entries.Hive Mind: Gestalt consciousness: pops are drones, no consumer goods, unity from synapse jobs.
entries.Machine Intelligence: Gestalt robots: energy instead of food, no consumer goods, pop assembly instead of growth.
entries.Bio-Trophy: Organic pops kept by Rogue Servitors to generate Unity. Protect them.
entries.Menial Drone: Worker-stratum drone in a gestalt empire.
entries.Complex Drone: Specialist-stratum drone in a gestalt empire.
entries.Synth: Synthetic (robot) population. Synth Ascension = upload your species into robots.
entries.Psionic: Ascension path: commune with the Shroud for powerful but risky bonuses.
entries.Cybernetic: Ascension path: bolt augments onto your existing pops, keep their traits.
entries.Genetic / Erudite: Ascension path: rewrite your species' traits directly.
entries.Mutation: Ascension path (BioGenesis): random beneficial mutations, flexible and chaotic.
entries.Cloning: Ascension path (BioGenesis): clone vats, extreme pop growth.
entries.Purity: Ascension path (BioGenesis): maximise a chosen species trait line.
entries.Modularity: Machine ascension: ships/pops get modular traits you can swap.
entries.Nanite: Machine ascension: turn planets into nanite worlds, swarm everything.
entries.Virtuality: Machine ascension: very few colonies, each pop is extremely efficient.
entries.Ascension Perk: A permanent empire-wide bonus unlocked by finishing a Tradition tree. Max 8 (or more with mods).
entries.Tradition Tree: One of several trees (Expansion, Discovery, Domination, etc.) bought with Unity. Finishing one unlocks an Ascension Perk slot.
entries.Become the Crisis: Ascension perk: you become the end-game crisis and fight the whole galaxy for Menace.
entries.Menace: Resource generated by the Become the Crisis perk; spent on ships and powers.
entries.Colossus: A planet-killer ship unlocked by the Colossus Project perk. Required for Total War.
entries.Total War: War goal with no peace until one side is wiped out. Needs Colossus or a genocidal civic.
entries.Casus Belli: Your legal reason for war. Determines what wargoal you can push.
entries.Claims: Marks on systems you want. Conquering unclaimed systems in a claim war costs you.
entries.War Exhaustion: 0-100% meter. At 100% you can be forced into Status Quo peace after a grace period.
entries.Status Quo: Peace that leaves each side holding whatever they currently occupy and have claimed.
entries.Choke Point: A system with only one or two hyperlane exits. Fortify these - it is your border.
entries.Bastion: Starbase building type: guns, hangars, and an FTL inhibitor to trap enemies.
entries.FTL Inhibitor: Starbase module that stops enemy fleets jumping out of the system once engaged.
entries.Naval Cap: Naval Capacity - fleet size limit. Going over it costs escalating Alloy upkeep.
entries.Command Limit: Max ships a single fleet can hold under one admiral.
entries.Starbase Cap: How many upgraded starbases you can maintain. Over cap = brutal energy upkeep.
entries.PD: Point Defense - weapons that shoot down missiles and strike craft. Bring some vs. hangars.
entries.Flak: Point-defense variant good against strike craft.
entries.Disruptor: Weapon that bypasses shields and armour straight to hull. Great early, weak vs. shields late.
entries.Arc Emitter: A penetrating X-slot weapon that ignores shields and armour entirely.
entries.Tachyon Lance: Long-range X-slot beam, huge damage, long cooldown.
entries.Giga Cannon: Long-range X-slot kinetic, huge damage vs. hull.
entries.Kinetic Artillery: Long-range L-slot kinetic - the backbone of artillery battleship fleets.
entries.Neutron Launcher: Long-range L-slot energy weapon with bonus vs. armour.
entries.Strike Craft: Fighters/bombers launched from hangar slots. Countered by PD/flak.
entries.Evasion: Chance a ship avoids a hit. Corvettes have lots, battleships almost none.
entries.Disengagement: Chance a damaged ship escapes instead of exploding. Saves you alloys over a long war.
entries.Emergency FTL: The mechanic that lets a damaged ship jump out - that is disengagement.
entries.Corvette Spam: Flooding the map with cheap evasive corvettes. Strong early, falls off late.
entries.Monofleet: A fleet of only one ship type, usually all-battleship artillery.
entries.Tech Rush: Beeline research: labs early, be first to the important techs.
entries.Unity Rush: Beeline Unity: traditions and ascension perks as fast as possible.
entries.Tall: Few planets, very developed. Relies on habitats, ecumenopoleis and vassals.
entries.Wide: Lots of planets and systems. More raw output, more empire-size penalty.
entries.Empire Size: Formerly Sprawl - total size of your empire. Over 100 it raises research and tradition costs.
entries.Sprawl: Old name for Empire Size. If you see it in a guide, it means Empire Size.
entries.Admin Cap: Old name for the Empire Size limit, now called Administrative Efficiency.
entries.Bureaucrat: Job that produces Administrative Efficiency to offset empire size. Now often 'Administrator'.
entries.Unity: Resource used to buy Traditions. Comes from factions, priests, culture workers, autochthon monuments.
entries.Influence: Resource used for claims, edicts, diplomacy and expansion. Mostly from factions and power projection.
entries.Alloys: The ship/construction resource. The single most important strategic resource for war.
entries.Consumer Goods: CG - upkeep for your pops' standard of living. Run out and happiness tanks.
entries.EC: Energy Credits - the generic currency for upkeep, markets and the Galactic Market.
entries.Trade Value: Money produced by clerks/merchants that must be routed home by trade routes or it is lost to piracy.
entries.Trade Route: The path trade value takes back to your capital. Unprotected routes spawn pirates.
entries.Amenities: Quality-of-life on a planet. Too few = unhappy pops and lower stability.
entries.Stability: 0-100% planet score that scales all planet output. Low stability is the usual cause of a bad colony.
entries.Habitability: How well your species lives on a planet type. Below 100% it cuts output and pop growth.
entries.Devastation: War damage on a planet. Slows everything until it is repaired.
entries.Crime: Pops steal and form criminal syndicates. Countered by enforcers and precincts.
entries.Pop Growth: How fast new pops appear. The core long-term growth engine of any empire.
entries.Pop Assembly: Building pops instead of growing them - robots, clones. Runs alongside natural growth.
entries.Strata: Pop class: Ruler / Specialist / Worker (or the gestalt equivalents). Determines political weight.
entries.Ruler: Top stratum - administrators, nobles, high-priests. High upkeep, high political power.
entries.Specialist: Middle stratum - researchers, metallurgists, artisans. The backbone of a real economy.
entries.Worker: Bottom stratum - farmers, miners, technicians. Cheap, mass employment.
entries.Unemployed: Pops with no job. They drain resources and become unhappy - build districts or jobs.
entries.Resettlement: Manually moving pops between planets. Costs energy and influence unless automatic.
entries.Auto-Resettlement: Pops migrate to available jobs by themselves. Needs a policy or transit hubs.
entries.Purge: Forcibly removing unwanted pops. Options range from displacement to processing.
entries.Slavery: Living standard that boosts worker output at the cost of happiness and stability.
entries.Living Standard: How well your pops live - drives consumer-goods upkeep and happiness.
entries.Faction: A political bloc in your empire. Approval from happy factions gives Unity and Influence.
entries.Ethics: Your empire's beliefs (militarist, xenophile, materialist...). Drives factions and diplomacy.
entries.Gestalt Consciousness: Hive minds and machine intelligences: no ethics, no factions, no happiness.
entries.Authority: Government type: Democratic, Oligarchic, Dictatorial, Imperial, or gestalt variants.
entries.Council: Your leader cabinet. Council seats give empire-wide bonuses and agendas.
entries.Agenda: A passive empire bonus chosen from the council. Completing it gives Unity.
entries.Edict: A temporary empire-wide buff with upkeep. Limited number active at once.
entries.Sector: A group of planets for a governor. Mostly automated once capitals are set.
entries.Designation: The role you give a planet (Forge World, Agri-World, Tech World) for bonuses.
entries.Planetary Automation: Lets the AI build on your planets. Convenient but often wasteful - review it.
entries.Blocker: A tile obstacle on a planet you pay to clear. Some give bonuses when cleared.
entries.District: Planetary zone (city, mining, generator, agriculture, industrial) that creates jobs.
entries.Building: A structure on a planet that adds specific jobs or bonuses. Limited slots.
entries.Anomaly: A researchable oddity found while surveying. Big source of early research.
entries.Dig Site: Archaeological site - a multi-stage excavation that yields relics or bonuses.
entries.Relic: A unique powerful item or activation from archaeology or an event.
entries.Minor Artifacts: Currency from archaeology used to activate relics and buy curator boons.
entries.Zro: Rare strategic resource tied to the Shroud and psionics.
entries.Dark Matter: Late-game strategic resource from black holes. Best reactor and shields.
entries.Nanites: Strategic resource (Nemesis) for nanite edicts and ship components.
entries.Living Metal: Strategic resource from special deposits. Strong ship components and edicts.
entries.Exotic Gases: Strategic resource. Needed for advanced research labs and many buildings.
entries.Volatile Motes: Strategic resource. Needed for many advanced buildings and ship components.
entries.Rare Crystals: Strategic resource. Needed for advanced buildings and some components.
entries.Betharian: A rare planetary deposit that powers a very strong generator plant.
entries.Precursor: An ancient civilisation whose chain of anomalies you can follow for a big reward.
entries.Cybrex: Machine precursor - rewards a ring world segment. Favoured by gestalts and materialists.
entries.Zroni: Psionic precursor - rewards psionic boosts. Pairs with Teachers of the Shroud.
entries.First League: Precursor that rewards an ecumenopolis start via the Arcology Project.
entries.Yuht: Precursor that rewards unity and a unique building.
entries.Baol: Precursor that gives terraforming and a gaia-world-related prize.
entries.L-Gate: A network of gates. Opening it early is a classic way to ruin (or win) a game.
entries.Grey Tempest: What sometimes comes out of the L-Cluster. Nanite ships that eat the galaxy.
entries.Terminal Egress: The L-Cluster's central system - the exit point for whatever is inside.
entries.Gateway: Buildable instant-travel network. The single biggest quality-of-life and strategic upgrade.
entries.Shroud: The psionic dimension. Covenants give great bonuses and occasional disasters.
entries.Crisis: The end-game catastrophe: Unbidden, Prethoryn Scourge, Contingency, Cetana, or a player.
entries.Unbidden: Extradimensional invaders from a rift. Shield-heavy, weak to shield-piercing weapons.
entries.Prethoryn Scourge: Bugs. Armour/health heavy, eat planets. Weak to energy weapons.
entries.Contingency: Rogue AI that hijacks machine pops and your own ships. Weak to shields.
entries.Cetana: The end-game crisis of The Machine Age - a vast machine intelligence with a unique mechanic.
entries.Great Khan: Mid-game event: marauder fleets unite and rampage. Survive him and you get a bonus.
entries.Marauder: Raider empires you can hire, bribe, or eventually conquer for a big satrapy.
entries.Enclave: Neutral space station you trade favours with: Curators, Artisans, Traders, Shroud-Touched.
entries.Curator: Enclave that sells research boosts and minor-artifact boons.
entries.Artisan Troupe: Enclave that sells unity/amenities boosts and art monuments.
entries.Caravaneer: Roving trader fleet that visits your systems selling odd goods.
entries.Satrapy: A special subject type you get by conquering marauders.
entries.Vassal: A subject empire that gives you resources and joins your wars.
entries.Protectorate: A pre-FTL or weak subject you protect until they advance.
entries.Tributary: A subject that pays you a share of their economy but keeps independence.
entries.Subsidiary: A specialised subject under Overlord, focused on one output.
entries.Bulwark: Subject type (Overlord) that specialises in military and gives you bonuses.
entries.Prospectorium: Subject type (Overlord) that pays you a large share of basic resources.
entries.Scholarium: Subject type (Overlord) that pays you research.
entries.Hegemony: Federation type where one leader dominates and can drag members into war.
entries.Federation: An alliance with shared fleets and levels. Very strong in the mid/late game.
entries.Espionage: Operations, assets and infiltration. Used for intel, sabotage and stealing tech.
entries.Intel: How much you know about another empire. Unlocks more diplomatic and spy options.
entries.First Contact: Dealing with pre-FTL or newly-met empires. Choose your posture carefully.
entries.Pre-FTL: A species that has not reached space yet. Observe, infiltrate or enlighten.
entries.Situation: A tracked multi-stage event chain shown in the situation log. Usually has choices and a timer.
entries.Council Agenda: The passive bonus your council is currently pushing.
entries.Vault: Where relics and artifacts are stored and activated from.
entries.Ship Designer: The screen where you build ship templates from hulls, sections and components.
entries.Auto-Design: Lets the AI update your ship templates. Usually worse than a hand-built design.
entries.Fleet Manager: The screen to build, reinforce, and merge fleets. Always reinforce before a war.
entries.Hyper Relays: Buildable relay network that lets fleets travel without returning to a starbase.
